what.text: Piracetam (2-oxo-1-pyrrolidine acetamide) is a small synthetic molecule. It is not a peptide. Its UK label classes it as a nootropic (ATC code N06BX03). Australia's Poisons Standard groups it with related drugs as "racetams".

what.text: In the UK it is a licensed medicine, Nootropil, for adults with myoclonus (jerking movements) that starts in the brain's cortex, used with other anti-myoclonus drugs. In Belgium and Luxembourg, Nootropil is a prescription medicine for memory or intellectual problems of brain origin without dementia, and for cortical myoclonus.

items.text: It is almost fully absorbed when taken by mouth and crosses into the brain and the placenta. It leaves the body through the kidneys.

research.text: Piracetam has been tested in many trials, mostly in older people with dementia or memory problems, and in stroke. Reviews disagree: a maker-funded analysis found a global benefit, while Cochrane and a 2024 review found no clear effect on memory or thinking.

research.title: Dementia or cognitive impairment, Cochrane 2001

facts.v: Flicker L, Grimley Evans G. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2001;(2):CD001011
review of randomized, placebo-controlled trials, including unpublished studies supplied by UCB
people with Alzheimer's, vascular or mixed dementia, or cognitive impairment
global impression of change, cognition and other measures

research.found: More people improved on global impression with piracetam (odds ratio 3.55 in one model), but results varied widely between trials, and effects on cognition were inconclusive. The reviewers wrote that the evidence "does not support the use of piracetam" in dementia or cognitive impairment.

clinical global impression of change

research.found: The authors report a difference favouring piracetam on global impression.

research.title: Memory in adults with memory problems, 2024

facts.v: Gouhie FA, et al. Clin Neurol Neurosurg 2024;243:108358
review of trials comparing piracetam with placebo
18 studies, 886 patients, 442 on piracetam
memory

research.found: No clear difference in memory (standardized mean difference 0.75, 95% CI -0.19 to 1.69), with very large differences between studies (I² 96%). The authors said the effect on memory cannot be determined.

research.title: Acute ischaemic stroke, Cochrane 2012

facts.v: Ricci S, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;(9):CD000419
review of randomized trials starting within three days of stroke
3 trials, 1,002 patients aged 40 to 85; one trial gave 93% of the data
death, function, dependence

research.found: A non-significant rise in death at one month with piracetam (about 31%), which disappeared in the large trial after correcting for stroke severity. No difference in function or dependence in limited data. Adverse effects were not reported.

us.text: Piracetam is not FDA approved for any use. FDA has cited products containing piracetam, many sold as dietary supplements, as unapproved new drugs and/or misbranded drugs. FDA lists piracetam as nominated for compounding without adequate support. As of November 1, 2026.

world.lead: Piracetam is a licensed prescription medicine in the UK, Belgium and Luxembourg (Nootropil), with different approved uses. It is prescription-only in Australia but not authorized there. It is not approved in the US or Canada. WADA does not name it, but names a close relative, fonturacetam.

side.text: From the UK label: nervousness, hyperkinesia (overactivity) and weight gain are common. It can affect blood clotting and is not for people with brain bleeding, Huntington's chorea or severe kidney failure. Stopping suddenly can trigger seizures in people with myoclonus.

unconfirmed: FDA's 2004 response to a new dietary ingredient notification for piracetam, which press reports say found it is not a dietary ingredient, could not be opened (regulations.gov limited automated requests).
The full text of the 2019 JAMA Internal Medicine study on piracetam in supplements could not be opened, so its findings are not reported.
EMA's page on the Nootropil referral returned an error (too many requests) and was not used.
National approvals in EU countries other than Belgium and Luxembourg, and the TGA's product register, were not checked.
surprises: Piracetam is sold in the US as a memory supplement, but in the UK its only licensed use is cortical myoclonus, and Cochrane found the evidence does not support its use in dementia or cognitive impairment.
A 676-person, 12-month maker-sponsored trial in mild cognitive impairment finished in 2004 but has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
